name: The Finer Holm Oak of Edinburgh Gardens

location.address: Edinburgh Gardens, near the bowling club, off Brunswick Street, Fitzroy North VIC 3068

verified_sources: City of Yarra Significant Trees register (data/registers/melbourne-yarra-significant-trees.json, ref 120)
https://trusttrees.org.au/tree/VIC/Fitzroy_North/Edinburgh_Gardens_Brunswick_Street (National Trust of Australia Vic, Significant Tree Register)
access: Free, always open. Public City of Yarra park, 24 hectares, unrestricted access per the National Trust record.
transport: Rushall railway station (Mernda line) is about a 3 minute walk from the gardens; tram route 11/112 runs along nearby St Georges Road.
verify_notes: One of two Holm Oaks in Edinburgh Gardens (the other is Yarra register ref 119, dbh 145cm, ~65m away, sent to leads); the National Trust of Australia (Vic) register independently lists this one as 'the finer of two examples of the species in the Gardens', confirming it at essentially the same coordinates (within 5m of the Yarra register point) with diameter ~2m and height ~20m, matching the register's dbh 177cm (=1.77m diameter, circumference approx 5.56m) and height 20m closely. TWO INDEPENDENT SOURCES for existence, species and location; age is register-only ('100+ years', last surveyed 2012-08-16, so at least 14 years have passed since, hence age_min 114). Flag: the National Trust's 2011 survey recorded this tree's condition as 'Poor', noting it is 'overcrowded by nearby Elms' -- worth a line on the page rather than hiding it; not evidence of death, but worth monitoring. Edinburgh Gardens was granted by Queen Victoria in 1862 and holds one of the most significant stands of mature elms in the world (Dutch elm disease never reached Australia). Statement of significance also references Talindert at Camperdown as holding the largest known example of the species in Victoria, useful comparison line for the story.

name: The English Elm of Darling Gardens

location.address: Darling Gardens, off Gold Street, Clifton Hill VIC 3068

verified_sources: City of Yarra Significant Trees register (data/registers/melbourne-yarra-significant-trees.json, ref 1)

National Trust of Australia (Vic) Significant Tree Register, cited via search snippet (trusttrees.org.au covers Darling Gardens; direct fetch not completed this pass) and corroborated by Collingwood Historical Society, https://collingwoodhs.org.au/darling-gardens-clifton-hill-52103/
access: Free, always open. Public City of Yarra park (also used as an off-leash dog area, does not restrict general access).
transport: Clifton Hill railway station (Hurstbridge/Mernda lines) is about a 6 minute walk; tram route 86 on Queens Parade is about a 6 minute walk (24-Gold St/Queens Pde stop).
verify_notes: TWO INDEPENDENT SOURCES for existence and age: the Yarra register (dbh 154cm = diameter 1.54m, circumference approx 4.84m, height 28m, category '100+ years', surveyed 2012-08-16) and the National Trust of Australia (Vic) Significant Tree Register, which independently dated this elm at approximately 120 years old as of February 2011 (so roughly 135 years old today) and calls it an 'outstanding example of the species'. FLAG: species name conflict between sources -- the Yarra register records it as Ulmus minor 'Atinia' (True English Elm cultivar) while the National Trust summary found via search names it Ulmus procera; both are commonly called 'English Elm' and the discrepancy could not be resolved to the primary National Trust page this pass (search snippet only, direct trusttrees.org.au URL for this specific tree not located). Darling Gardens was permanently reserved in 1866 and is one of three former City of Collingwood sites on the National Trust Tree Register, laid out in the 1890s with elms and oaks. Also on-site: Darling Gardens' Holm Oak, ref 2, delivered separately as mel_004.

name: The Moreton Bay Fig of Curtain Square

location.address: Curtain Square, Canning Street entrance, Carlton North VIC 3054

verified_sources: City of Yarra Significant Trees register (data/registers/melbourne-yarra-significant-trees.json, ref 180)
City of Yarra Heritage Review, Landscape Citations (local significance listing for Curtain Square, referenced via search; full citation PDF not fetched this pass)
access: Free, always open. Public City of Yarra park (also used as an off-leash dog area).
transport: Curtain Square/Rathdowne St bus stop is directly outside; tram route 96 on Nicholson Street is roughly a 5-10 minute walk.
verify_notes: Curtain Square (1.46 ha) was a bluestone quarry worked by convicts from the Collingwood Stockade 1853-1866, then filled and planted; an avenue of Moreton Bay Figs 'remains at the Canning Street entrance' per local sources, which this tree (dbh 152cm = diameter 1.52m, circumference approx 4.77m, height 25m) is very likely part of. Existence and public-park status independently corroborated (heritage citation + local history), but the specific age figure ('100+ years', surveyed 2012-08-16) is register-only, hence flagged. Context worth keeping for the writer: in Sept 2017 the square's separate north/south avenue of elms (some ~100 years old) was removed for public safety and replaced with scarlet oaks -- this fig was not part of that removal and is a different avenue/species, but it is a live example of how exposed even 'significant' trees are, worth a line about ongoing stewardship rather than permanence.

name: The Osage Orange of Yarra Boulevard

location.address: Yarra Boulevard, near the Swan Street connection, Yarra Bend Park, Burnley VIC 3121

verified_sources: City of Yarra Significant Trees register (data/registers/melbourne-yarra-significant-trees.json, ref 227)

Victorian Heritage Database, 'The Boulevard Parklands' citation (vhd.heritagecouncil.vic.gov.au/places/103863), cited via search: an Osage Orange 'situated ... to the north-east of the connection of Yarra Boulevard to Swan Street is listed on the Significant Tree Register', 'dating back to the 1860s'
access: Free, always open. Public parkland along Yarra Boulevard, part of Yarra Bend Park / the Boulevard Parklands, a well-used shared walking and cycling corridor along the Yarra River.
transport: No tram or train stop immediately adjacent. Reachable via the Yarra River shared path or Yarra Boulevard itself; the nearest railway stations (Burnley, Victoria Park, or East Richmond) are roughly 2km away by path.
verify_notes: TWO INDEPENDENT SOURCES: the Yarra register (dbh 169cm = diameter 1.69m, circumference approx 5.31m, unusually tall for the species at height 27m, age category '100+ years', surveyed 2012-08-16) and the Victorian Heritage Database's 'Boulevard Parklands' citation, which independently names an Osage Orange at this stretch of Yarra Boulevard and dates it to the 1860s planting era (so roughly 160 years old today, notably older than the register's coarse '100+' bucket suggests, not a conflict, just more specific). Osage Orange is an unusual, distinctive species for the area, which makes the match between the two sources fairly safe even though the two records were not pixel-matched by coordinate. This is the anchor tree of a second, more distant cluster (Yarra Bend Park / the Boulevard Parklands, roughly 6-7km from the Edinburgh Gardens/Darling Gardens/Curtain Square cluster, too far to walk between the two in one outing). Yarra Boulevard was built as Depression-era public works and is aesthetically significant in its own right. The park was created as a Depression-era public-works boulevard along the Yarra.
